pos.personaBrief: The Danubian passing heritage Bukovi 'perfected' and the Wembley display ('interchanging forwards, a mingling of short and long passes', Hidegkuti's goal after a ten-pass sequence) describe a side that wanted the ball and controlled games with it.

pro.personaBrief: Build-up mixed swift short passing and positional interchange with long cross-field balls (FA Year Book 1953, Nemzeti Sport 2006), with Bozsik organising and Hidegkuti directing play from deep, so patient combination with a ready long option.

est.personaBrief: Strongly relational: the withdrawn centre-forward dropping and drifting to the wing, forwards 'continually swapping positions', wingers slotting into midfield and Buzanszky's 'We did not have fix positions'.

lar.personaBrief: The danger came centrally (inside forwards Puskas and Kocsis as strikers, Hidegkuti pulling the centre-half out, four of six Wembley goals from outside the box), though wingers and full-backs pushed on gave width as support.

blo.personaBrief: No pressing fact exists; Puskas's 'in defence it was the same' suggests collective defending, while Lorant staying deep as almost a sweeper and Zakarias dropping in for cover point to a team that regrouped rather than hunted high, as in that era.

mar.personaBrief: Hungary's own marking is not described; the WM tradition they came from was man-oriented (stopper on the centre-forward), so a man-oriented back line is the likely inference.

pla.personaBrief: A fixed identity built over 'three years' work' with a club-bloc squad and imposed by the coaches, though Sebes did change tactics during games (Switzerland 1952, Italy 1953) that then became the identity.

res.personaBrief: An attacking ideal of 'jogo bonito, em detrimento de qualquer tatica defensiva' (Guttmann) and an elegant, ball-control style remembered beyond the 1954 final defeat, under a regime that also demanded wins.

sis.personaBrief: A collective system (club-bloc chemistry, 'everyone attacked, everyone defended', defined roles like Hidegkuti's) that still relied on stars such as Puskas, Kocsis and Hidegkuti to make it work.

jog.personaBrief: Technique first ('speed, ball control, and positional play', 'ball control amounting to elegance') joined to superior fitness that Sebes and Guttmann demanded; Guttmann even signed a 35-year-old Zizinho.

bas.personaBrief: The squad was assembled by moving established players to Honved and MTK and Guttmann asked for the veteran Zizinho; no youth-development fact is in the period.

lid.personaBrief: Authoritarian regimes (Sebes's rigorous fitness and strict timetable, Guttmann's strict diet and quitting when Puskas overruled his substitution), tempered by tactical discussions where Puskas and senior players contributed.
